title: Tuesday Teacher Plan
note: Blooket opener. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket. 6th and 7th: no tape; hand out the Joints That Hold card.

4th Period.topic: Strategy pattern, Day 2: plan your moving brick
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can plan my moving brick: which row gets the slide strategy, how fast it moves, and what changes every frame.
4th Period.exitTicket: Your plan: which row slides, at what speed, and what changes every frame?
prep: Day 2 handout attached to the Strategy Pattern assignment
Exit ticket posted with both sentence frames
Frame-trace table drawn on the board (startX 100, speed 2)

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Monday: what a strategy is, update(), the brick factory.
tips: Load the grade's Blooket_*_Tue_Nov3 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, I can plan my moving brick: which row gets the slide strategy, how fast it moves, and what changes every frame.
segments.why: Students know the target before work starts.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: I do: stayStill vs. slide
segments.do: Read both strategies from the handout. Key rule: each brick measures from its OWN startX, so the whole row turns together and nothing overlaps.
segments.why: Worked example before the plan (gradual release).
tips: Ask: what would go wrong if bricks bounced off the walls instead? (The end brick turns first; the rest slide into it.)

segments.title: We do: trace one brick
segments.do: On the board, students call out x after each frame. Frame 16: x reaches 132, distance 32 is over 30, speed flips to -2.
segments.why: Tracing builds the mental model before Wednesday's trace and Thursday's build.
tips: Cold call after think time; have partners agree first.
Faster speed = turns around more often.

segments.title: You do: plan the moving brick
segments.do: Students play their game 1 minute, pick a row (0-3) and a speed (1-3), say the plan to a partner, partner checks row + speed + what changes.
tips: Undecided: row 0, speed 1.
No code changes today.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: The plan is the exit ticket, on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: a row number, a speed, x changes by the speed every frame, turns around 30 px from startX.

watchFor: Students starting to code: plan only today.
Plans with no row or no speed.

6th Period.topic: Warren Truss Build, Day 2: side truss 2 (one strike)
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group has built side truss 2 to match side truss 1 exactly, and joined both sides with cross pieces if we had time.
6th Period.exitTicket: When you stacked side 2 on side 1, did they match? Why do both sides of a bridge need to match?
prep: Day 2 handout attached to today's exit ticket
One Joints That Hold card per table
Side truss 1 and drawings handed back
Cardboard, paper, glue sticks, scissors per table. No tape.
The 5 one-strike rules on the board

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Monday: measuring stick, the drawing, check before gluing, glue squares, cut length, the one-strike rules.
tips: Load the grade's Blooket_*_Tue_Nov3 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, my group has built side truss 2 to match side truss 1 exactly, and joined both sides with cross pieces if we had time.
segments.why: Students know the target before work starts.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Roles by birthday + the 5 rules
segments.do: Same roles as Monday: youngest Builder, 2nd youngest Cutter, 2nd oldest MM, oldest Checker. Repeat the 5 rules chorally.
segments.why: Complex Instruction + clear limits before materials come out.

segments.title: You do: build side truss 2 on the drawing
segments.do: Bottom chord, 6 diagonals, top chord, each cut, checked on the drawing, glued with the 4 glue steps. If time: 4 cross pieces with fold-over tabs.
segments.why: Bloom Apply; the drawing makes every piece checkable.
tips: Walk the room the whole time. Call a strike at once, calmly.
Flat truss = face-on-face glue squares, which hold. Cross pieces are the 90-degree problem: tabs or slots.
Praise precise Checkers publicly (assign competence).

segments.title: Check: stack side 2 on side 1
segments.do: Checker stacks the sides; fix anything off before it dries.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: whether they matched (or where they didn't), plus that matching sides keep the bridge straight and share the load evenly.

segments.title: Clean up + set to dry
segments.do: Scraps in the bin, scissors counted, both sides flat on the shelf.
tips: Count scissors.

watchFor: Cross pieces glued edge-on: steer to fold-over tabs.
Groups breaking a rule: Chromebooks (Truzme) for the week.

7th Period.topic: Bridge Deck and Load Test, Day 2: fix joints, finish deck, roof
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, every joint on our bridge passes the Checker's tug test, our deck is finished, and we have started the roof: cross pieces on the top joints and an X-brace in each box.
7th Period.exitTicket: Which joint technique did your group use today, and why does it hold better than gluing an edge?
prep: Day 2 handout attached to Bridge Deck and Load Test
One Joints That Hold card per table
Scrap paper for wraps, cardboard, glue sticks, scissors. No tape.
Before class: make one fold-over tab and one paper wrap yourself to show

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Monday: bottom joints, deck on the joints, 1/4 stick apart, glue test, cross pieces.
tips: Load the grade's Blooket_*_Tue_Nov3 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, every joint on our bridge passes the Checker's tug test, our deck is finished, and we have started the roof: cross pieces on the top joints and an X-brace in each box.
segments.why: Students know the target before work starts.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Why the glue let go: turn edges into faces
segments.do: Show a glue stick on a cardboard edge vs. a fold-over tab and a paper wrap. Key rule: glue sticks hold faces, not edges. Point to the 6 techniques on the card.
segments.why: Turn yesterday's failure into the lesson (Maslow: failure is safe, and expected).
tips: Ask: why did the glue fail? Let students explain it first.

segments.title: Roles by birthday
segments.do: Youngest Deck Finisher, 2nd youngest Roof Builder, 2nd oldest Materials Manager, oldest Checker. Group of 3: Checker also MM. Group of 5: two Roof Builders.

segments.title: You do: tug test, fix joints, finish deck
segments.do: Checker tug-tests every joint; loose ones get paper wraps or L-brackets. Every deck stick gets a paper wrap under it and up both faces of the bottom chord.
segments.why: A solid deck matters most for Wednesday's Test 1.
tips: Score folds with a closed scissor blade.
Rub paper wraps flat for 30 seconds.

segments.title: You do: twist test, roof, twist test again
segments.do: Gentle twist before (a lot / a little / not at all). Cross pieces on the 3 top joints with tabs folded down outside the top chords. X-brace in each roof box, measured on the bridge. Twist again.
segments.why: Rigor for this class: a before/after test of one change.
tips: Many groups won't reach the roof: that's expected; tomorrow's test still works.
X-brace stops racking: the box can't turn into a parallelogram.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: names a technique (tab, paper wrap, L-bracket, gusset, slot, shaped end) plus that it gives the glue a flat face to hold instead of a thin edge.

segments.title: Clean up + set to dry
segments.do: Bridge flat on the shelf, scraps in the bin.
tips: Count scissors.

watchFor: Anyone reaching for tape: no tape.
Paper wraps that only touch one piece.
Roof tabs folded inward (they go on the outside).

accommodations: Goal reviewed after the Blooket and at the exit ticket; numbered steps; worked examples (slide strategy, Joints That Hold card); checklists; two sentence frames.
Pictures for every key word (strategy, startX; tab, wrap, gusset, face vs. edge); partner talk before writing; choral rules in 7th.
Lexend Deca; steps read aloud; speech-to-text OK; spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer; hands-on roles (Builder, Checker, Roof Builder); tug and twist tests are movement; break pass.
Dictated exit tickets; extended time. Floors: 8th names a row and a speed; 7th glues the bottom chord and 2 diagonals; 6th fixes 2 joints with paper wraps.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL), 1 KB point: 8th a 3rd strategy; 7th gussets or slot joints; 6th portal brace or gussets.
frameworks: Every grade moves its product forward: a planned moving brick, a second side truss, a braced bridge.
Birthday-order roles with real authority (Checker approval and tug test); praise precise work publicly.
Yesterday's glue failure is named and fixed, not blamed; one turn-in; 'you are not behind'.
8th Apply (plan); 7th Apply (build to match); 6th Apply/Analyze (fix, then test a change).
